prompt: An active mid-rise construction site in a Denver neighborhood: a concrete and steel frame five stories up, a tower crane, chain-link fence with torn green privacy screening, a gravel gate with a small site trailer, stacked materials and a parked excavator, mud and tire ruts, older brick buildings and the foothills behind. Light: a flat, overcast winter day, soft gray sky, patchy old snow along the curbs. A documentary photograph taken by a working photographer in Colorado, not an architectural showcase: eye level, from across the street or the edge of the lot, 35mm lens, ordinary unposed framing. Real-world wear everywhere: weathered concrete, dust, tire marks, dry grass and weeds at the edges, faded paint lines, utility poles and wires, a few ordinary parked cars. Natural, uneven light with no glow, no lens flare, no HDR look, no hyper-clean surfaces, no perfect symmetry. Muted, true-to-life color like an unedited RAW file, fine grain, slightly imperfect exposure. The main subject sits in a horizontal band through the middle of the frame, near the center, so the picture still works cropped to a wide strip or to a tall 4:5 crop. Wide 16:9. No people in uniform and no recognizable people, no readable text, signs, logos, flags, insignia, or watermarks. Not any real, identifiable building. Use the reference photos only for their photographic look: lens, light, color, realism, and the Colorado setting. Do not copy their buildings, mountains' exact shapes, signs, or any text.
